drivers.name: Real interest rates (US 10-year TIPS yield)
drivers.reading: The 10-year real yield is 2.67%, down 23bp over the past month. Gold pays no interest, so a higher real yield raises the cost of holding it: rising real yields are a headwind for gold and falling ones a tailwind. gold-events finds the link is not stable: gold's sensitivity to real yields was near zero before 2013, strong in 2014-2021 and weaker now.

drivers.name: The US dollar (broad trade-weighted index)
drivers.reading: The dollar index is up 1.0% over the past month. Gold is priced in dollars, so a weaker dollar makes it cheaper for buyers paying in other currencies and tends to lift its dollar price; a stronger dollar does the reverse.

drivers.name: War and political tension (Geopolitical Risk index)
drivers.source: Caldara and Iacoviello, Geopolitical Risk Index
drivers.reading: The index averaged 181 over the past week (100 is the 1985-2019 average), higher than 88% of days in the past ten years. Gold often gains when tension spikes because investors buy it as a store of value outside the financial system. gold-events finds the index helps explain gold's weekly moves alongside real yields and the dollar, and that its effect has grown since 2020.

drivers.name: Central-bank gold buying (IMF reporters)
drivers.source: IMF International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity (IRFCL)
drivers.reading: Central banks reporting to the IMF added 272 tonnes in the 12 months to 2026-09, against 295 tonnes in the 12 months before. Official buying is demand that does not depend on interest rates; gold-events finds last month's buying does not help predict next week's move, so read it as background, not a timing signal. The latest months are incomplete until every reporter files, so they understate buying.

model.note: Expected move over the next 5 trading days from the frozen gold-events model (v2-rolling): its regression on last week's changes in real yields, the dollar, VIX and the Geopolitical Risk index. The model predicts log returns; shown here as percentage changes. Out of sample it has been scored on 0 weeks so far.

recent.note: prediction uses last week's control changes as the coming week's input

upcoming.title: US midterm elections
upcoming.summary: All 435 House seats and a third of the Senate are elected; the result decides which party controls each chamber of Congress.
upcoming.what_to_watch: Which party controls the House and the Senate, and how real yields and the dollar react in the days after. gold-events' study of every midterm since 2002 gives the average gold move afterwards (below).

study.note: Average gold move after every US midterm since 2002 (1994 and 1998 lack data); net = after removing the part explained by the dollar and real yields over the same days. gold-events' verdict: one or two years drive the averages, so there is no reliable midterm effect.

upcoming.title: FOMC rate decision and projections
upcoming.what_to_watch: The rate decision and the statement. A cut, or a signal that cuts are coming, tends to lower real yields and weaken the dollar, which supports gold; a hawkish surprise does the opposite. This meeting also publishes the Fed's economic projections, including the 'dot plot' of expected rates.
